newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Plains fed cattle market tone weak - feedlots.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Plains fed cattle market tone weak - feedlots.

text.p: U.S. Plains feedlot cattle near midday Monday sold in thin activity at lower prices, but volume was too light to test the market, feedlot sources said.

Less than 1,000 heifers that will likely grade select and choice sold at $64.00 per cwt in Kansas, down $1.00 from brisk sales late Friday, sources there said. There were no reported sales in the Texas Panhandle/western Oklahoma area.

Remaining bids at $64.00 were light and many were passed by owners pricing cattle mostly at $65.00 to $66.00, with a few at $67.00. Friday's late sales at $65.00 were down $1.00 from thin volume earlier in the week, cattle feeders said.
The late Friday sales helped keep many feedlots current in their marketings but demoralized owners who had been holding out for $66.00, sources said.
Sales at $65.00 were at unprofitable levels for most cattle owners who need $66.00-$68.00 to break even, they said.
"Some of these guys lost a good chunk of money," one Kansas feedlot manager said.
Fed cattle prices were pressured by a buildup of beef which packers had to discount to encourage movement, the sources said.
